newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral wants good ties with S.Asia.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral wants good ties with S.Asia.

text.p: Prime minister-designate Inder Kumar Gujral said on Sunday that he would continue to try to improve relations with India's South Asian neighbours while defending an independent foreign policy.

Gujral, who was foreign minister in the outgoing government of caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, told Reuters Television in an interview that he would pay keen attention to relations with the major world powers.
"As foreign minister, I have built some sort of a doctrine regarding neighbourly relations. That will continue to be my priority area," said Gujral.

"I am equally keen that our relations with the major world powers -- Europe, America, China, Russia -- continue to get my attention," he said, adding that Indian foreign policy must remain independent.

Earlier on Sunday, parliamentarians from the United Front coalition unanimously elected Gujral to be their leader, endorsing the choice late on Saturday of the alliance's decision-making Steering Committee.

Gujral was scheduled to meet President Shankar Dayal Sharma at around 0530 GMT to stake his claim to form a new centre-left government. It was not known when he and his cabinet, yet to be announced, would be sworn in.
